o1.biggest_strength: It spots the in-app checkout bug as a fix, not a test, sizes the money well, and then ranks sensible tests tied tightly to the data.
o1.biggest_mistake: It uses arbitrary calendar dates and runs some overlapping tests that would need careful interaction checks; I would remove the dates unless they match our real calendar.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the assumed dates with week numbers, tighten the parallel-test plan, and add a little more around firmness as its own buyer concern rather than mostly through reviews.

o2.biggest_strength: It is very usable for a small team: clear bug-first call, clean funnel read, practical ship-now list, and ranked tests with good metrics and guardrails.
o2.biggest_mistake: The simultaneous test schedule is a little hand-wavy: saying paired tests each get all the traffic needs a clearer factorial or lane setup, and combining image plus reviews makes the result less diagnostic.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Spell out the testing lanes more rigorously, keep reviews and hero separate if traffic allows, and add projected business value for each test like it does for the checkout bug.

reason: I would rather hand Output 1 to the team because it is a bit more commercially sharp: it sizes the bug, gives stronger MDE detail per test, and has more ready-to-build copy. Output 2 is also strong and slightly cleaner, but Output 1 feels a little closer to an action plan.
